legal.scope: Internal enterprise use of React Doctor as an isolated, optional static provider behind Web Doctor, for developers and coding agents
conditions: Use React Doctor only inside the enterprise; never sell it or offer it to third parties as a paid, hosted, or managed product or service whose value derives substantially from it

Never use React Doctor, its source code, derivative works, or its output as training, fine-tuning, or evaluation data for a machine-learning model or AI system, or as input to a pipeline that trains or improves one, without prior written permission from Million Software, Inc.
Keep React Doctor's copyright notice and Modified MIT License with every installed copy

security.scope: The React Doctor scan command, run by the Web Doctor adapter in a bounded Node process under the permission model
conditions: Run only the scan command with the configuration below; never run install, ci, scan <url>, rules set, rules enable, rules disable, rules category, rules ignore-tag, or audit mode, which write to the application, its CI, its agent configuration, or its source
Grant no network: telemetry to Sentry and Axiom, the score and share API, and Socket.dev supply-chain lookups stay disabled by flags and are blocked by the network guard
Refuse an application with an executable doctor.config file, because loading it would run repository code in a process that may start child processes
Refuse an application with leftover .react-doctor/audit-backups, which React Doctor would restore into source files
Write only to a private scratch directory and to the absent .react-doctor/audit-backups path, and pass no PATH, so git, bash, and nvm cannot be started
Pin exactly one release per entry; a new release needs its own entry, digests, contract tests, and evaluation
